about: A woman is written 'Zephra Quillon' with three 'she' and 'Zephra' alone with two: neither spelling is a strong pronoun case, five of five pooled is. A model that is unsure of the short form leaves one person with two genders unless the spellings share their evidence.
title: The Net Loft
author: Ada Pell

chapters.title: Tide
paragraphs: Zephra Quillon opened the net loft before the tide turned. She hung the dry nets on the long pegs.
Halvard came in with the first basket of the day. He set it down by the scale and said nothing.
Zephra counted the baskets twice. She wrote the number on the slate with a stub of chalk.
Zephra Quillon sorted the catch by size. She threw the small ones back into the bucket.
Halvard weighed the largest fish on the brass scale. He grunted at the number and wrote it down.
The gulls wheeled over the quay and complained. A cart stood at the end of the planks with its shafts in the air.
Halvard hauled the empty baskets back to the boat. He stacked them in the stern, one inside the other.
Zephra mended a torn net by the open door. She knotted the cord with quick, practised fingers.
Halvard tied up the boat and checked the lines. He tested each knot with his thumb before he left it.
Zephra Quillon locked the loft at dusk and hung the key on its nail. She walked home along the sea wall.
Halvard sat on the quay and watched the last light go. He waited for the night boat as he did every evening.
Halvard carried the lamp to the end of the planks. He held it high so the night boat could find the landing.
Halvard coiled the rope at the foot of the post. He hung the lamp on its hook for the morning.
Halvard shut the gate of the quay behind him. He looked back once at the dark water.
In the village everyone knew Zephra Quillon, and nobody had a bad word for Zephra Quillon.
Years afterwards people still asked about Zephra Quillon, though few could say why.

In the village everyone knew Halvard, and nobody had a bad word for Halvard.
Years afterwards people still asked about Halvard, though few could say why.
